task.description: REWORK ITERATION 1: SECURITY-REVIEWER FAILed Step 2c with a BLOCKER on INV-1 (docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md), root-caused in this design. Read handoffs/WF02-REQ037-20260817/step-02c-security-reviewer.json's full result.summary and result.issues[0] for the complete finding before touching the design doc. Summary: insert_review/2's design (lib/letflow/design/promotion_review_state_machine.md lines ~337-339) explicitly specifies that attrs.tenant_id is set from the caller-supplied plan.target_tenant_id while opts[:prefix] is taken as an independently-trusted value with nothing tying the two together -- this is exactly the rejected option (a) from docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md's 2026-08-17 write-time tenant_id-derivation addendum. The addendum's own accepted resolution is to derive/validate tenant_id from opts[:prefix] via Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 (already shipped, built for REQ-025 -- read that function's actual signature/behavior directly, don't assume). Read the addendum in docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md in full to understand exactly what it requires. Revise ONLY the insert_review/2 section of the design (§2.3) to close this gap: either (a) derive tenant_id internally from opts[:prefix] via tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 rather than trusting plan.target_tenant_id at all, or (b) validate that plan.target_tenant_id matches the tenant_id derived from opts[:prefix] and return an explicit error (name the atom) on mismatch before any insert -- pick whichever the addendum actually calls for (read it, don't guess), and state your reasoning. The other 5 transition functions were confirmed by SECURITY-REVIEWER to be safe (they never touch the tenant_id column, only read via prefix-scoped Repo.get) -- do not unnecessarily change them, but do double check them explicitly against the addendum for completeness in your revised doc. promote_definition/3's own design is otherwise unaffected -- do not revise it unless the insert_review/2 fix changes what it can trust from review.tenant_id.
acceptance_criteria: Revised design's insert_review/2 satisfies the 2026-08-17 write-time tenant_id-derivation addendum to Decision 0003 -- explicitly cite which of the addendum's accepted resolutions you applied and why
No other function's design changed unless the insert_review/2 fix requires it, and any such change is called out explicitly
The revision is scoped to the design doc only -- do not touch implementation files (ELIXIR-DEV re-implements after this passes validation again)

Explicitly re-verify the other 5 transition functions against the addendum in the revised doc, even though SECURITY-REVIEWER already confirmed them safe, so the doc's own reasoning is complete and self-contained

result.summary: Revised lib/letflow/design/promotion_review_state_machine.md §2.3 (insert_review/2) to close the SECURITY-REVIEWER BLOCKER. Read docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md's 2026-08-17 addendum in full: it names three candidate mechanisms for populating a write-time tenant_id column and adopts exactly one -- option (c), 'Derive it from the resolved schema at write time' -- rejecting option (a) 'caller supplies tenant_id as an explicit parameter' (the shape the failed design used) for its attribution-integrity gap, and deferring option (b) session-GUC context as out of scope. Applied (c), not a validate-and-reject hybrid (that is not one of the addendum's three named options): insert_review/2's algorithm now has a new step 3 that calls Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix) (read directly at lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:100-115 -- pure, no I/O, {:ok, tenant_id} | {:error, :invalid_schema_name}) and uses that derived value for attrs.tenant_id at step 4; args.plan.target_tenant_id is no longer read for this purpose at all (not even for a mismatch check, since the adopted resolution is derivation, not validation of a caller-supplied value). insert_review_error's type gained :invalid_schema_name (the function's actual error atom) and dropped the unused :invalid_tenant_id placeholder. This exactly mirrors Letflow.EventStore.append/2's already-shipped precedent for the same addendum (lib/letflow/event_store.ex:9-18, 'tenant_id is always derived from opts[:prefix] ... never accepted from attrs'). Added new §2.8 ('2026-08-17 addendum compliance -- explicit re-verification, all 6 functions') with a table showing each of the other 5 transition functions' exact set:/attrs list from its own section, confirming none assigns to the tenant_id column at all (they only ever set status/approved_by/approved_at/superseded_by/row_version), so the addendum -- which governs who computes a written tenant_id value -- is structurally not-applicable to them, not merely 'checked and found safe' by assertion. Also corrected two downstream inconsistencies the fix created: §3.2 step 1's note on review.tenant_id being 'a trusted, typed value' now explains why it's trustworthy (derived at insert_review/2 time, not caller-supplied), and §8's cross-module dependency list, which previously stated PromotionReviewStore has no direct dependency on Letflow.TenantProvisioning, now records the new tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 dependency insert_review/2 introduces. Added INV-PRM04-6 to §6 restating the derived-not-accepted rule as a standing invariant. No implementation files touched -- design doc only. No function other than insert_review/2 had its algorithm changed; promote_definition/3's own algorithm is unchanged (only its rationale comment for step 1 was clarified to explain why review.tenant_id is now genuinely trustworthy).
